_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS R1206's CONTRACT IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
WHAT THE CONTRACT IS. `scripts/fmt.sh` must WRITE every package manifest
`scripts/check-side-workspaces.sh` CHECKS, and the root workspace besides.
It derives that population from the gate's own `--list` rather than keeping
a second list, so the law it has to hold is easy to state and easy to make
vacuous by accident: two programs that agree because neither was asked.
SO EACH INJECTION BREAKS ONE WAY THE FIXER COULD STOP COVERING THE CHECKER,
and each of the three is a thing that would otherwise be silent. A dropped
workspace leaves a file the repository can reject and cannot fix. A `--check`
left on leaves a command that reports exactly like one that formatted and
wrote nothing. A missing root leaves the half that was already working.
RUN IT LOCALLY. The harness edits this tree and writes the firing record
beside this file, so a run sent to a build machine leaves its evidence on a
throwaway copy — measured in R1205, which is why that round's carry names

injections.name: the-formatter-stops-reaching-a-workspace
injections.why: the failure the two-population arrangement had by default and nothing noticed: a workspace the gate checks that the fixing command never reaches, so the repository can REJECT a file it has no command to fix. `bench` is the one used here because it is nine of the twenty-seven manifests, and a drop that size is still invisible to a person reading a green run

injections.name: the-formatter-checks-instead-of-writing
injections.why: the one failure that looks EXACTLY like success: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo fmt` differ by a flag and by everything, and a fixer that kept the flag would exit 0 on a formatted tree, print the same lines, and write nothing at all. The check-that-is-not-checking refusal in the script is the mirror of this, and this is the direction with no message of its own

injections.name: the-formatter-forgets-the-root
injections.why: the half that already worked, and therefore the half a repair is most likely to drop while its author is watching the other one. `cargo fmt --all` is the ONLY thing covering the root workspace's members here, and nothing in the side gate would notice its absence — the root is exactly what that gate deliberately does not read
